column1: What does BM25 do that dense embedding retrieval cannot?
column2: BM25 matches exact tokens by term frequency — catching proper nouns, ticker symbols, and entity names that dense embeddings may miss through semantic generalization.

column1: What is Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) used for in hybrid retrieval?
column2: RRF merges ranked lists from BM25 and dense retrieval by summing reciprocal ranks for each document, producing a single merged ranking that benefits from both sparse and dense signals.

column1: What does a cross-encoder reranker do differently than a bi-encoder?
column2: A cross-encoder sees the query and document concatenated together, producing a calibrated relevance score. It is more accurate than cosine similarity but requires O(N) forward passes — one per candidate document.

column1: What is contextual retrieval and what improvement does it provide?
column2: It prepends LLM-generated context describing each chunk's role in the full document before embedding. Anthropic reported a 49% reduction in retrieval failures (Sept 2024).

column1: What is HyDE and when should you avoid it?
column2: HyDE generates a hypothetical answer to the query and embeds that instead of the raw query. Avoid it on domain-specific entity questions where the LLM may confabulate wrong facts, drifting the embedding from true relevant documents.

column1: Name the four metrics RAGAS measures.
column2: Context precision, context recall, faithfulness (answer claims grounded in context), and answer relevancy (answer addresses the question).

column1: Why is it wrong to measure only end-to-end accuracy for a RAG system?
column2: The four RAGAS metrics fail independently. A system can be faithful but miss relevant chunks (high faithfulness, low recall) or retrieve correctly but hallucinate from the correct context. Collapsing to one metric erases diagnostic signal.

column1: What query type does GraphRAG specifically outperform dense retrieval on?
column2: Global sensemaking questions requiring cross-document entity resolution and aggregation — e.g., 'Which portfolio founders have prior exits?' — where dense retrieval cannot aggregate across all documents.

column1: What is the practical cost of building a GraphRAG index over 500 VC memos?
column2: Roughly 1,000 LLM calls for entity extraction (~$5 at GPT-4o mini pricing) plus offline graph construction (Leiden community detection) and storage in a graph database or parquet format.

column1: What is the parent-document retrieval pattern and why is it useful?
column2: Index small child chunks for retrieval precision, but return the full parent section (e.g., the full financial section of a memo) when a child chunk matches. This preserves retrieval precision while giving the LLM sufficient context to answer.
